final_candidate.name: span_to_bottleneck_ratio
final_candidate.hypothesis: For a fixed framework bottleneck (lsd_f), adsorbates with a larger heavy-atom enclosing radius (SPAN) experience tighter geometric confinement at pore windows and along free paths, which restricts translational and reorientational freedom of the adsorbed molecule; therefore Sads decreases and the entropy loss (Sgas - Sads)/R increases with SPAN/lsd_f. Equivalently, holding SPAN fixed, frameworks with larger lsd_f impose weaker confinement and smaller entropy loss.
final_candidate.rationale: SPAN is a heavy-atom enclosing radius (implicit-H representation, legitimate zeros for monatomic/point cases) and is not a full all-atom molecular size; lsd_f is the Zeo++ Df largest passing sphere, a bottleneck proxy for a fixed geometric probe and NOT a global cavity diameter. The ratio is a dimensionless size-to-bottleneck confinement proxy: it is a shape/connectivity coupling heuristic commonly motivated in confinement arguments, but neither the restriction of adsorbed-phase motion by pore windows nor a monotone entropy-loss dependence on this ratio is verified in this dataset. AV is mass-specific fixed-probe accessibility, not molecule-specific free volume, so the ratio is used as a pure geometry coupling term rather than a free-volume estimate. No target values were used; the direction of the effect is an empirical hypothesis to be tested.
final_candidate.falsification_criteria: The hypothesis is falsified if, holding lsd_f fixed, predicted entropy loss does not increase with native SPAN over the training span of the ratio (SPAN/lsd_f ranging roughly from 0 to ~7.3 within training support), or if the dependence is flat/insensitive. A competing explanation would be that apparent sensitivity is actually driven by co-varying framework accessibility (AV or ASA) rather than by the bottleneck coupling; if entropy loss decreases with SPAN at fixed lsd_f, an alternative packing/entropy-gain mechanism would be indicated.
final_candidate.proxy_assumptions: Assumes (i) heavy-atom SPAN is an adequate molecular size proxy despite implicit hydrogens, (ii) Df bottleneck governs adsorbed-phase mobility, (iii) confinement effect on entropy scales with the dimensionless size/bottleneck ratio, and (iv) adsorption proceeds through channels characterized by Df. These are proxy assumptions, not established causality.
final_candidate.boundary_behavior: Finite training support: SPAN in [0, 6.2408] angstrom with 54 legitimate zeros preserved (descriptor value 0 for monatomic cases, not imputed); lsd_f in [0.85684, 7.68726] angstrom is strictly positive, so the ratio is finite and well-defined everywhere in the training domain; no division-by-zero occurs.

review_issues.explanation: SPAN is a heavy-atom enclosing radius computed in the original implicit-H/heavy-atom representation, not full all-atom molecular geometry. For hydrogen-containing adsorbates the numerator systematically understates the physical molecular size, so the ratio is a size proxy with representation-dependent bias; the magnitude of this bias for adsorbed-phase confinement is unquantified.

lsd_f is the Zeo++ Df largest passing free sphere along a periodic free path, a bottleneck proxy for a fixed geometric probe. The hypothesis text extends it to confinement 'at pore windows and along free paths', but the free-sphere path is a graph-theoretic construct that need not coincide with the actual diffusion or adsorption pathway of a real molecule; Df is explicitly NOT a global cavity diameter Di.

The dimensionless ratio SPAN/lsd_f couples two different geometric conventions: a heavy-atom molecular radius against a probe-based framework bottleneck. The ratio is a heuristic coupling term; no established physical scaling law states that adsorbed-phase entropy loss scales monotonically with this particular ratio.

The monotone-increasing claim (entropy loss rises with SPAN at fixed lsd_f, and falls with lsd_f at fixed SPAN) is an unverified empirical hypothesis. No target values are provided and no evidence supports the direction; derivative/limit checks are numerical execution checks only and do not validate the mechanism (execution_check.mechanism_validated is false).

The hypothesis asserts a single monotone regime over the full training ratio range (~0 to ~7.3). When SPAN/lsd_f < 1, the molecular enclosing radius is smaller than the largest passing sphere, i.e. geometrically unconstrained passage; a confinement mechanism would predict qualitatively different (possibly negligible) entropy-loss sensitivity in that sub-regime. A global monotone form across both sub-regimes is an assumption not established by any recorded evidence.

The falsification criteria acknowledge a competing explanation: apparent sensitivity to SPAN/lsd_f may be driven by co-varying framework accessibility (AV, ASA) rather than the bottleneck coupling. AV is mass-specific fixed-probe accessibility, not molecule-specific free volume, so neither the primary mechanism nor the alternative is distinguishable without target data.

SPAN has 54 legitimate zeros (consistent with the 54 single-site rotor cases), giving descriptor value 0 for those samples. The zero is representationally valid, but the physical interpretation of a zero confinement ratio for point-like/monatomic adsorbates versus an unconstrained small molecule is not distinguished by the descriptor; the hypothesis text does not state how the mechanism behaves at ratio exactly 0.

The recorded limit test only covers lsd_f -> +infinity (ratio -> 0). The limit as lsd_f approaches its training minimum (0.85684 angstrom) with SPAN at maximum (6.2408 angstrom) yields a ratio of ~7.28; behavior beyond training support (lsd_f -> 0, ratio -> infinity) is undefined and no saturation or physical bound on the descriptor is specified.

No evidence_ids are cited and no target values are provided in the inputs. The mechanism (bottleneck confinement restricts translational/reorientational freedom, lowering Sads) is a plausible literature-style argument but is unsupported by any source in the record; the direction of the effect is explicitly an untested empirical claim.

Graph support between SPAN, lsd_f, and the target is unknown. Absent edges in any recorded dependency structure are unknown relationships, not disproof of the confinement proxy; conversely, no recorded edge substantiates the mechanism either.

review_issues.explanation: Unit heterogeneity by construction: the numerator Vol is angstrom^3 per molecule, while the denominator AV + AV_ref is cm^3/g of framework. The ratio is not dimensionless, and its numerical value depends on the arbitrary unit convention (1 angstrom^3 = 1e-24 cm^3). Only monotone-ordering claims are invariant to this convention. The execution_check output_dimensions entry (framework_mass '1') does not follow from the expression as written; passing the dimension check does not validate the cross-unit ratio.

Per-molecule vs per-mass mismatch: Vol is a single-molecule quantity and AV is mass-specific. A true packing fraction would require an adsorbate loading (molecules per gram framework), which is not among the available inputs. The hypothesis text describes an 'effective packing fraction', which overstates what the expression computes; the draft rationale concedes this, but the hypothesis still asserts the packing mechanism as the operative effect.

variable_mappings includes AV_ref, which is not a native input but a fixed additive constant; this likely relates to the execution_check rejection ('Mappings must match exactly the actual proxy inputs'). Additionally, the additive offset use of AV_ref differs from the defined q-normalization (q_X = X/X_ref), so the offset is an empirical smoothing choice. Note the cited AV_ref = 0.0759781 matches the stats 'ref' field but differs from the AV training median (0.0748459); the offset value is an empirical constant, not a measured quantity.

AV = 0 handling: the +AV_ref offset assigns the 28 probe-closed training frameworks the descriptor maximum (Vol/AV_ref), i.e., the highest predicted entropy loss. Whether fixed-probe-closed frameworks truly have maximal molecular entropy loss is an extrapolation of the monotone proxy assumption into a regime the fixed probe cannot rank. The values are finite and non-imputed (legitimate zeros preserved), but their physical interpretation is unverified.

The limit_test varies AV toward positive infinity, far outside the training support (AV max 0.661336 cm^3/g); the limit value 0 is mathematically correct but physically unreachable. There is also an internal inconsistency: the limit test varies AV while expression_check specifies regime_input Vol, so the two checks exercise different axes of the descriptor.

Directional claims (Sads decreases with Vol/(AV + AV_ref); entropy loss increases with Vol at fixed AV, and decreases with AV at fixed Vol) are asserted as a crowding mechanism, but no evidence_ids or independent source support is provided; physical_claims lists only 'empirical_proxy'. The stated falsification criteria are appropriate and testable, but the hypothesis as written reads as established mechanism rather than an untested empirical hypothesis.

request.task: ONE technical repair only. Preserve proxies, hypothesis and physical predictions. Non-equivalent formula changes require a scientific revision and are forbidden here.

LabuteASA.meaning: Labute approximate molecular surface area of the adsorbate.

PBF.meaning: Mean atom distance from the best-fit molecular plane; measures planarity.
PBF.representation: Original implicit-H/heavy-atom representation; legitimate zero values. Not full all-atom molecular geometry.

PMI1.meaning: First principal moment of inertia of the adsorbate.
PMI1.representation: Original implicit-H/heavy-atom representation; legitimate zero values. Not full all-atom molecular geometry.

PMI2.meaning: Second principal moment of inertia of the adsorbate.
PMI2.representation: Original implicit-H/heavy-atom representation; legitimate zero values. Not full all-atom molecular geometry.

PMI3.meaning: Third principal moment of inertia of the adsorbate.
PMI3.representation: Original implicit-H/heavy-atom representation; legitimate zero values. Not full all-atom molecular geometry.

SPAN.meaning: Radius enclosing all molecular atoms about the center of mass.
SPAN.representation: Original implicit-H/heavy-atom representation; legitimate zero values. Not full all-atom molecular geometry.

GeDi.meaning: Largest distance between two molecular atoms.
GeDi.representation: Original implicit-H/heavy-atom representation; legitimate zero values. Not full all-atom molecular geometry.

Vol.meaning: Van der Waals volume of the adsorbate molecule.

density.meaning: Framework density on the published numerical scale; physical unit unresolved.

ASA.meaning: Framework surface area accessible to a probe, per framework mass.

AV.meaning: Framework volume accessible to a probe, per framework mass.
AV.zero_meaning: Zero accessibility for the fixed geometric probe does not imply zero physical molecular adsorption space.

lsd_f.meaning: Zeo++ Df: largest sphere able to pass through a periodic free path; bottleneck proxy, NOT global cavity diameter Di.

lsd_p.meaning: Zeo++ Dif: largest included sphere ALONG the free-sphere path; NOT bottleneck Df and NOT necessarily global cavity Di.

notes: Positive reference medians DO NOT remove input zeros.
Use full-domain finite proxies or explicit rotor_case branches; no median imputation of physical zeros.
Independent q-normalization does not turn one into a physical equality threshold.
All statistics and reference values use training features only.

prior_formulas.hypothesis: For a fixed framework bottleneck (lsd_f), adsorbates with a larger heavy-atom enclosing radius (SPAN) experience tighter geometric confinement at pore windows and along free paths, which restricts translational and reorientational freedom of the adsorbed molecule; therefore Sads decreases and the entropy loss (Sgas - Sads)/R increases with SPAN/lsd_f. Equivalently, holding SPAN fixed, frameworks with larger lsd_f impose weaker confinement and smaller entropy loss.

For a fixed passing bottleneck (lsd_f), a larger included-along-path sphere (lsd_p) indicates that the free diffusion path traverses progressively more spacious cavities behind the tight windows; a molecule that has passed the bottleneck therefore gains additional translational and reorientational freedom inside the pore segment, raising Sads and reducing the entropy loss (Sgas - Sads)/R. Equivalently, holding lsd_p fixed, a larger lsd_f means the narrowest constriction is itself wider, weakening confinement and decreasing the entropy loss. The ratio lsd_p/lsd_f thus separates channel-like pores (ratio near 1, weak spatial contrast) from cage-window architectures (large ratio, strong confinement contrast at windows).

request.target_definition: entropy_loss_over_R=(Sgas-Sads)/R; ANN predicts Sads/Sgas. Loss is NOT -log(Sads/Sgas). No target values are provided.
request.normalization: q_X=X/X_ref, fixed positive reference from training features. Native zeros remain valid; q_X is not X_ref.
formula_rules: Use native inputs, q_NAME, NAME_ref, fixed constants; + - * / **, log log10 sqrt abs exp minimum maximum; no indexing or imports. Fixed numerical exponents in [-8,8].
D0 already contains all fourteen inputs. A formula re-expresses information, not a new observation.
Logs/exp require dimensionless arguments; explicit rotor_case for native single-site/linear/nonlinear inertia.
No gas entropy, labels, fitted constants, scores, target correlations, imports or IDs as formula inputs.
Passing Df is not cavity Di; included-along-path Dif is not the passing bottleneck.
AV is mass-specific fixed-probe accessibility, not molecule-specific free volume.
Hold other actually used native inputs fixed in the conditional physical prediction.
Do not copy a previously appended descriptor. Duplicates occupy the slot and will not be resampled.
Unknown graph support is allowed; absent edge does not disprove a proxy or mechanism.
State empirical choices and unverified mechanisms honestly. Structured limits may be empty.

draft.name: adsorbate_volume_per_accessible_specific_volume
draft.hypothesis: For a fixed accessible specific pore volume (AV), an adsorbate with larger van der Waals volume (Vol) occupies a larger fraction of the framework's probe-accessible space; this higher effective packing fraction reduces the configurational and translational freedom available to the adsorbed molecule, so Sads decreases and the entropy loss (Sgas - Sads)/R increases with Vol/(AV + AV_ref). Conversely, holding Vol fixed, frameworks with larger AV offer more accessible space per unit mass, weakening crowding and decreasing the entropy loss.
draft.rationale: This descriptor couples the adsorbate's molecular_vdw_volume with the framework's probe_accessible_specific_volume, targeting a packing/crowding mechanism distinct from the bottleneck-confinement descriptor (SPAN/lsd_f) and the cage-window-contrast descriptor (lsd_p/lsd_f). Known proxy limitations: (1) AV is a mass-specific fixed-geometric-probe accessibility, not molecule-specific free volume — the descriptor is an empirical crowding proxy, not a true packing fraction; (2) AV = 0 for the fixed probe does not imply zero physical molecular adsorption space, so the +AV_ref offset keeps the expression finite and defined at legitimate zeros rather than introducing a threshold interpretation; (3) Vol is an all-atom VdW volume while the geometric shape proxies are heavy-atom-based, so Vol and the geometry descriptors are not interchangeable; (4) the units of Vol (angstrom^3) and AV (cm^3/g) are heterogeneous, so the numerical scale is empirical and unit-inconsistent by construction — only the monotone ordering is claimed. The crowding mechanism is a plausible but unverified hypothesis; it is stated as empirical_proxy, not established causality.
draft.falsification_criteria: If, within frameworks of matched AV, the entropy loss (Sgas - Sads)/R does not increase with Vol (or decreases), the crowding hypothesis fails. If, within adsorbates of matched Vol, larger AV does not reduce entropy loss, the accessibility-side mechanism fails. If AV = 0 (fixed-probe-closed) frameworks show entropy losses indistinguishable from high-AV frameworks at the same Vol/(AV + AV_ref) value, the descriptor's accessibility interpretation is falsified. A competing explanation: any apparent correlation could be driven by lsd_f or lsd_p alone (correlated pore-size axes); if Vol/(AV + AV_ref) loses all conditional association after holding lsd_f and lsd_p fixed, the descriptor adds no mechanism beyond round-1 and round-2 confinement descriptors.

variable_mappings.AV_ref: fixed positive training reference for probe_accessible_specific_volume

draft.proxy_assumptions: Assumes the fixed-probe accessible specific volume AV tracks, monotonically, the space physically available to real adsorbate molecules of varying size; assumes Vol scales the excluded volume the adsorbate contributes inside that space; assumes both map monotonically onto reduced translational/configurational freedom of the adsorbed phase. None of these is established causality; each is an explicit empirical proxy assumption.
draft.boundary_behavior: Finite on full training support: Vol in [20.424, 161.144] angstrom^3 and AV in [0, 0.661336] cm^3/g with AV_ref = 0.0759781 > 0, so the denominator is strictly positive and legitimate AV zeros (28 frameworks) are preserved as finite values (Vol/AV_ref at AV = 0), not imputed; no division by zero and no log/exp dimensionality issues.

appended.name: span_to_bottleneck_ratio
appended.hypothesis: For a fixed framework bottleneck (lsd_f), adsorbates with a larger heavy-atom enclosing radius (SPAN) experience tighter geometric confinement at pore windows and along free paths, which restricts translational and reorientational freedom of the adsorbed molecule; therefore Sads decreases and the entropy loss (Sgas - Sads)/R increases with SPAN/lsd_f. Equivalently, holding SPAN fixed, frameworks with larger lsd_f impose weaker confinement and smaller entropy loss.
appended.rationale: SPAN is a heavy-atom enclosing radius (implicit-H representation, legitimate zeros for monatomic/point cases) and is not a full all-atom molecular size; lsd_f is the Zeo++ Df largest passing sphere, a bottleneck proxy for a fixed geometric probe and NOT a global cavity diameter. The ratio is a dimensionless size-to-bottleneck confinement proxy: it is a shape/connectivity coupling heuristic commonly motivated in confinement arguments, but neither the restriction of adsorbed-phase motion by pore windows nor a monotone entropy-loss dependence on this ratio is verified in this dataset. AV is mass-specific fixed-probe accessibility, not molecule-specific free volume, so the ratio is used as a pure geometry coupling term rather than a free-volume estimate. No target values were used; the direction of the effect is an empirical hypothesis to be tested.
appended.falsification_criteria: The hypothesis is falsified if, holding lsd_f fixed, predicted entropy loss does not increase with native SPAN over the training span of the ratio (SPAN/lsd_f ranging roughly from 0 to ~7.3 within training support), or if the dependence is flat/insensitive. A competing explanation would be that apparent sensitivity is actually driven by co-varying framework accessibility (AV or ASA) rather than by the bottleneck coupling; if entropy loss decreases with SPAN at fixed lsd_f, an alternative packing/entropy-gain mechanism would be indicated.
appended.proxy_assumptions: Assumes (i) heavy-atom SPAN is an adequate molecular size proxy despite implicit hydrogens, (ii) Df bottleneck governs adsorbed-phase mobility, (iii) confinement effect on entropy scales with the dimensionless size/bottleneck ratio, and (iv) adsorption proceeds through channels characterized by Df. These are proxy assumptions, not established causality.
appended.boundary_behavior: Finite training support: SPAN in [0, 6.2408] angstrom with 54 legitimate zeros preserved (descriptor value 0 for monatomic cases, not imputed); lsd_f in [0.85684, 7.68726] angstrom is strictly positive, so the ratio is finite and well-defined everywhere in the training domain; no division-by-zero occurs.

appended.name: cage_to_window_aspect_ratio
appended.hypothesis: For a fixed passing bottleneck (lsd_f), a larger included-along-path sphere (lsd_p) indicates that the free diffusion path traverses progressively more spacious cavities behind the tight windows; a molecule that has passed the bottleneck therefore gains additional translational and reorientational freedom inside the pore segment, raising Sads and reducing the entropy loss (Sgas - Sads)/R. Equivalently, holding lsd_p fixed, a larger lsd_f means the narrowest constriction is itself wider, weakening confinement and decreasing the entropy loss. The ratio lsd_p/lsd_f thus separates channel-like pores (ratio near 1, weak spatial contrast) from cage-window architectures (large ratio, strong confinement contrast at windows).
appended.rationale: lsd_f (Df) is only a bottleneck proxy and lsd_p (Dif) is only the largest sphere along that same free-sphere path; neither alone distinguishes a uniformly sized channel from a cage behind a tight window. Their ratio is a dimensionless shape/connectivity contrast that uses exactly the information already present in the two inputs without re-expressing a single quantity. Limitations: both descriptors come from a fixed hard-sphere probe geometry, so they do not encode framework chemistry, flexibility, or adsorbate-framework interactions; the mapping from geometric path contrast to adsorbed-phase entropy is a hypothesis, not an established relation. The ratio is undefined if lsd_f were zero, but lsd_f is strictly positive on the training support (min 0.85684 angstrom).
appended.falsification_criteria: The descriptor is falsified as useful if (i) entropy loss correlates only with the absolute bottleneck scale (lsd_f alone) and the ratio adds no conditional information when lsd_f is held fixed, or (ii) Dif and Df are so tightly coupled across the training frameworks that the ratio is effectively constant, carrying no architectural contrast. A competing explanation is that apparent ratio effects are confounded with total accessible volume (AV/ASA), which this descriptor does not control for.
appended.proxy_assumptions: Assumes the hard-sphere free path (Df) and the largest included sphere along it (Dif) jointly characterize the confinement contrast experienced by real adsorbates; assumes Dif >= Df for each framework so the ratio is >= 1 on physical structures; assumes adsorbed-phase entropy depends on geometric freedom along the accessible path and not only on the bottleneck itself. These are proxy assumptions, not established causality.
appended.boundary_behavior: Both inputs are strictly positive with finite training support (lsd_f in [0.85684, 7.68726] angstrom; lsd_p in [3.3452, 15.5604] angstrom), so the ratio is finite and well-defined over the full training domain; no zero-imputation or rotor_case branching is needed. Under the physical assumption Dif >= Df the ratio is bounded below by 1, though the raw training ranges alone do not guarantee this for every paired sample; the descriptor remains finite regardless.

appended.name: adsorbate_volume_per_accessible_specific_volume
appended.hypothesis: For a fixed accessible specific pore volume (AV), an adsorbate with larger van der Waals volume (Vol) occupies a larger fraction of the framework's probe-accessible space; this higher effective packing fraction reduces the configurational and translational freedom available to the adsorbed molecule, so Sads decreases and the entropy loss (Sgas - Sads)/R increases with Vol/(AV + AV_ref). Conversely, holding Vol fixed, frameworks with larger AV offer more accessible space per unit mass, weakening crowding and decreasing the entropy loss.
appended.rationale: This descriptor couples the adsorbate's molecular_vdw_volume with the framework's probe_accessible_specific_volume, targeting a packing/crowding mechanism distinct from the bottleneck-confinement descriptor (SPAN/lsd_f) and the cage-window-contrast descriptor (lsd_p/lsd_f). Known proxy limitations: (1) AV is a mass-specific fixed-geometric-probe accessibility, not molecule-specific free volume — the descriptor is an empirical crowding proxy, not a true packing fraction; (2) AV = 0 for the fixed probe does not imply zero physical molecular adsorption space, so the +AV_ref offset keeps the expression finite and defined at legitimate zeros rather than introducing a threshold interpretation; (3) Vol is an all-atom VdW volume while the geometric shape proxies are heavy-atom-based, so Vol and the geometry descriptors are not interchangeable; (4) the units of Vol (angstrom^3) and AV (cm^3/g) are heterogeneous, so the numerical scale is empirical and unit-inconsistent by construction — only the monotone ordering is claimed. The crowding mechanism is a plausible but unverified hypothesis; it is stated as empirical_proxy, not established causality.
appended.falsification_criteria: If, within frameworks of matched AV, the entropy loss (Sgas - Sads)/R does not increase with Vol (or decreases), the crowding hypothesis fails. If, within adsorbates of matched Vol, larger AV does not reduce entropy loss, the accessibility-side mechanism fails. If AV = 0 (fixed-probe-closed) frameworks show entropy losses indistinguishable from high-AV frameworks at the same Vol/(AV + AV_ref) value, the descriptor's accessibility interpretation is falsified. A competing explanation: any apparent correlation could be driven by lsd_f or lsd_p alone (correlated pore-size axes); if Vol/(AV + AV_ref) loses all conditional association after holding lsd_f and lsd_p fixed, the descriptor adds no mechanism beyond round-1 and round-2 confinement descriptors.
appended.proxy_assumptions: Assumes the fixed-probe accessible specific volume AV tracks, monotonically, the space physically available to real adsorbate molecules of varying size; assumes Vol scales the excluded volume the adsorbate contributes inside that space; assumes both map monotonically onto reduced translational/configurational freedom of the adsorbed phase. None of these is established causality; each is an explicit empirical proxy assumption.
appended.boundary_behavior: Finite on full training support: Vol in [20.424, 161.144] angstrom^3 and AV in [0, 0.661336] cm^3/g with AV_ref = 0.0759781 > 0, so the denominator is strictly positive and legitimate AV zeros (28 frameworks) are preserved as finite values (Vol/AV_ref at AV = 0), not imputed; no division by zero and no log/exp dimensionality issues.
